title: ModelFuzz adds execution-time guardrails for agent tool calls
friendlyTitle: ModelFuzz checks an agent’s tool call before it can do damage
summary: ModelFuzz is a new MIT-licensed Python project that combines a prompt-injection scanner with a decorator that checks tool arguments against policy before execution. It is designed to block actions such as data exfiltration through email or HTTP tools even after a model has been manipulated.
friendlySummary: ModelFuzz can test an agent for prompt-injection problems and check tool inputs before a command, email or web request runs.
whyItMatters: Filtering prompts is not enough when an agent can run commands or send data. Enforcing policy at the tool boundary creates a separate control point, though the young project and its default rules require careful testing against false positives, bypasses and each organisation’s threat model.
friendlyWhyItMatters: Even a tricked AI model can be stopped if software checks the final action. Test the tool carefully because simple rules can still miss attacks or block safe work.
